posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
Andar said:
savefolder to something restricted
Click to expand...
Yes, it's very likely related to that. Older, unlicensed versions created a project folder in:
homedrive:\Program Files (x86)\ASCII\RPG2000\
So when he migrated to the Steam version, he probably didn't change the folder, and the Steam version doesn't start in administrator mode.
When he migrated to RM2K3, he probably moved the project to:
homedrive:\Users\My Docs\RPG2000\
Remember that the save files for RM2K/2K3 are located in the same folder as the game's executable file

posts.author: Cherry
posts.body:
You still didn't specify the exact problem "this" refers to. The sentence "it stopped me from saving my progress" is not specific. What does that mean? Did somebody with a shirt that said "RPG Maker" on it break into your house and dragged you away when you trying to click "save"? Probably not, yet this would be one of infinite possible interpretations of that sentence. So, please explain what exactly you did, what exactly you expected to happen and what exactly happened instead.
Similarly, the sentence "The project is in a folder i made called RM2K." is not specific either. Did you burn it onto a CD and placed it in a physical
folder
on your bookshelf with a sticker "RM2K" on it? Again, probably not, but it is not clear from the sentence where that folder is located. Please specify the full path, e.g. "C:\blah\blah\RM2k".
What I'm trying to say here (same with my other post regarding your faceset issue) is that we are not psychic, if you don't share with us all the information relevant to your problem or the information you share is so unspecific that it becomes a puzzle more than a problem-solving process, we cannot help, and we are just wasting our time and constantly having to ask for more details, it's a frustrating process for both you
and
us. This is a common issue with people new to technical work trying to get help online, so don't feel too bad about it, just think about why it's causing friction and how to avoid it, so that we can all benefit from it.
This article
explains the issue (and solution) pretty well, even though some parts about it (such as showing your code) won't apply here, but they will apply to some extent when you are having issues with events, for example.

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
D:\Rm2k is a folder in the root directory, I assume it's not a portable hard drive...
In other words, what Andar said and I reaffirmed, you cannot save files directly without going through the confirmation window (administrative privilege).
Even if your user is the administrator, confirmation will always be requested when moving files, however, files generated by game functions cannot be created.
This is also the cause of the error in the editor; it created the map in a temporary folder and when trying to move it, this error occurred.
Please pay attention to this information and move the Rm2k folder to your user's Documents folder...

posts.author: Cherry
posts.body:
@Dev_With_Coffee
: No, the error is while saving the temporary copy, not the final map file.
@Invisnir
Thank you, this is exactly what we needed to understand the situation better!
Did you close the editor and restart it and it keeps happening, or did you keep it open since you opened this thread because you have unsaved work? I feel like something (maybe a "PC cleaning" tool?) removed the temp folder `C:\Users\fscos\AppData\Local\Temp\RPG_TEMP` in which RPG Maker keeps the unsaved map files. Now this is bad news because anything that you changed since the last save other than the map you currently have open will be lost because the files are no longer there. But you could at least save that current map if you manually recreated that folder `RPG_TEMP` within your temporary directory.
Can you please check whether the `RPG_TEMP` folder exists? If not, create it. If it
does
exist, we have some other type of problem, and we'll need to use the "Process Monitor" tool to debug it, but we'll cross that bridge when we come to it.
